enhancements.requirement: Session signing falls back to public development strings. Empty environment strings are also accepted because `??` does not reject them.
The Director proxy and Eve channel have a default basic-auth password.
Vercel gallery storage defaults to a SQLite file in the temporary directory. Data is neither durable nor shared between function instances.
Director limiting is per generated session in process memory. Studio requests a new session on each proposal.

Gallery creation/reporting has no visible rate limiting; several endpoints parse unrestricted bodies. Some size checks happen after reading the whole body. Analytics trusts Content-Length for its limit.
Gallery identity is a randomly minted browser cookie, not a recoverable account.
AI output is schema-validated but the server does not independently enforce the brief's requested constraints.
Artwork records still say review and usage approval are pending.
Fixtures directly copy Button, Switch, Accordion, and the recipe utility. They do not test actual registry installation or the full catalog.
Fixture pages render a small subset; the inspected Vite and Next pages do not import character CSS. A successful build can therefore hide visual failure.
`resolveAnuimeRecipe` returns class strings but does not itself activate the color scope or recipe mode. Installed output depends on surrounding CSS/theme setup.

Several component files use React hooks without a client directive; the Next fixture only exercises a client page. This alone is not proof of failure: `useId` and consuming boundaries need framework-specific verification.
`getUsageSnippet` mechanically generates `<Component recipe={...} />`; many components require labels, rows, columns, tabs, or children.
Standalone component installation only declares the recipe utility for inspected items; fonts and character styling require additional setup.
No demonstrated immutable release artifacts or consumer rollback workflow.
`validateAnuimeRecipe` checks supported values and completeness only. It has no actual compatibility/conflict rules.

Fixed per-character geometry in components can override the separate recipe shape dimension. Many fields use fixed heights instead of density styles. `calm` and `expressive` resolve to the same motion classes in the shared resolver.
Studio catalogs 52 IDs separately from registry inventory and excludes many newer UI items and blocks.
Gallery remix picks `entry.componentIds[0]`; Studio stores a single component ID.
Recent local saves contain only recipes, not named full Studio documents.
Global Cmd/Ctrl-Z interception also catches typing inside editable fields.
The storage-read error handler calls `localStorage.removeItem` without its own guard.
Zoom parsing accepts numeric strings but returns the original value; runtime data can remain a string despite `StudioZoom`.
PNG export serializes a DOM clone into SVG without collecting external CSS, computed styles, fonts, or form state.
Browser viewport controls and illustrative states do not constitute full interaction inspection.
The inspected native dialog has no explicit accessible name/description association.
Calendar's first date input has no individual label by default; a fieldset legend names the group. Tooltip describes a wrapper rather than ensuring the focusable trigger owns the association.
Navigation uses the fixed ID `anuime-mobile-navigation`; 59 block source files repeat `overview` and `details` IDs.
Tabs only handle left/right arrows and expose an uncontrolled default selection.
The data-table component is currently a semantic static renderer.
Toast is a single status element with optional dismissal, not a complete notification system. Calendar uses native date fields; combobox uses datalist.
Many new blocks place unrelated component examples in the same auto-fit grid. Checkout has no submission interface, and FAQ search includes a work-email field.
Fourteen block source files contain explicit no-op callbacks; only one contains `onSubmit`; only eleven contain a recipe prop.
Component-level props, sizing, labels, class overrides, controlled state, and ref behavior vary.
Native/custom input behavior and data assumptions need edge-case verification.
